minutes.headline: Consultants presented Lunenburg's draft master plan -- 8 goals, ~80 recommendations -- ahead of a December report; no votes held.
minutes.summary: This was the sixth and final public information session on Lunenburg's master plan, led by the steering committee chair, planning board chair Matt Brener, and consultants from OverUnder. The consultants walked through eight community-derived goals (housing options, farmland protection, small business support, open space/recreation, community gathering spaces, municipal building prioritization, school facilities, and resilient infrastructure) and roughly 80 supporting recommendations, then described a three-part implementation strategy (an implementation committee, a filter checklist, and an implementation table) before residents asked about the adequacy of public input and how town government might respond; the session then moved into hands-on breakout activities with no formal votes taken.

what_happened.line: Consultants presented Lunenburg's draft master plan -- eight goals and roughly 80 recommendations -- with a final report due in December.
The plan's implementation strategy pairs a new committee with a filter checklist and a table to prioritize recommendations.
Recommendations include a possible affordable housing trust, a farmland preservation fund, and a stormwater infrastructure fund, none funded yet.
A resident asked whether outreach for the plan reached enough residents, given low turnout at this final session.
No votes were taken; the session moved into breakout activities for further discussion.

why_it_matters: Any adopted housing trust, farmland fund, or stormwater fund would need its own town funding mechanism, which could reach a future town meeting warrant.
The plan's goals for schools, housing, and infrastructure could shape capital requests and budget priorities over the next decade.
